findings.finding: AGENTS.md directly contradicts CLAUDE.md (and the actual code) on a security-relevant fact: AGENTS.md's Trio-draft-rules paragraph states the pre-toss squad-lock 'is UI-only, not enforced by Firestore rules or a server check,' while CLAUDE.md says it 'is enforced both client-side (UI) and server-side, via firestore.rules' pre-toss write checks.' firestore.rules line 39 (comment: 'the real match doc (one extra read) so a client can't spoof toss time') and the `!hasTossPassed(...)` checks on create/update/delete confirm CLAUDE.md is correct and AGENTS.md is stale — it was never updated after the 2026-07-20 'Squad writes locked server-side via firestore.rules' change recorded in PROGRESS.md.
findings.notes: Confirmed by grepping firestore.rules for 'toss'/'lock' and cross-referencing PROGRESS.md's 'Squad writes locked server-side via firestore.rules (2026-07-20)' entry. Fix: update AGENTS.md's Trio draft rules paragraph to match CLAUDE.md exactly (or better, have AGENTS.md explicitly defer to CLAUDE.md for architecture facts so the two can't diverge again). An AI agent (Codex) reading only AGENTS.md today would wrongly conclude no server enforcement exists and could either duplicate the rules-side lock unnecessarily or, worse, remove/weaken it thinking it's dead code.

findings.finding: README.md self-contradicts on the same fact: the 'Trio Draft Arena' feature bullet (line 169) reads 'Squads lock 30 minutes before match start ("toss") — enforced client-side today (see Known Limitations)', but the 'Firestore Collections > userSquads > Write rules' section (line 414) correctly says 'firestore.rules enforces the 30-minute pre-toss lock, squad shape, and the denormalized fields — not just the UI.' The '(see Known Limitations)' pointer is also dangling: the 'Known Limitations / Not Yet Built' section (lines 518-524) no longer mentions client-side-only locking at all.
findings.notes: This is leftover text from before the 2026-07-20 server-side lock shipped (per PROGRESS.md) that was never swept when the rest of the file was updated. Fix: rewrite README.md line 169 to state the lock is enforced both client-side and server-side (mirroring line 414), and remove the dangling 'see Known Limitations' cross-reference.

findings.finding: Beyond the direct contradiction (phase07-001), AGENTS.md is missing several whole sections/facts CLAUDE.md has: (1) the `npm run test:rules` command is absent from AGENTS.md's Commands block entirely; (2) the entire 'Visibility toggle enforcement spans rules + two API routes, not rules alone' architectural paragraph is missing; (3) the entire '"What day is this" is canonicalized on India Standard Time' paragraph (getMatchDayIST, IST-anchored leaderboard math) is missing; (4) the 'Working with the project owner' section (Notion-update workflow) is entirely absent; (5) the Styling paragraph omits the text-meta/text-micro legibility floor, shortPlayerName(), and Sheet.tsx's dialog accessibility, listing only 3 of the 5 utils.ts helpers CLAUDE.md lists; (6) the Data flow/ETL paragraph omits the seriesId string-coercion and scripts/backfill-seriesid.mjs detail; (7) the Admin API auth paragraph omits that adminAuth.ts also exports requireAuth() for non-admin authenticated routes.
findings.notes: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md were clearly forked from the same source but AGENTS.md hasn't tracked at least four rounds of CLAUDE.md updates (IST work, visibility-toggle server-side fix, item #9 legibility pass, Notion workflow addition). Fix: either regenerate AGENTS.md from CLAUDE.md verbatim (they are word-for-word identical up through most of the file, suggesting a copy-then-diverge origin), or replace AGENTS.md's architecture content with a one-line pointer to CLAUDE.md to eliminate the drift surface going forward — CLAUDE.md's own line 11 already says 'Keep both README.md and this file current,' but doesn't mention AGENTS.md as a file needing the same discipline, which is likely why it was missed.

findings.finding: The submission-visibility-toggle reimplementation in `GET /api/leaderboard` and `GET /api/matches/[matchId]/squads` (src/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts, src/app/api/matches/[matchId]/squads/route.ts) — the app's core anti-collusion enforcement, and specifically called out in CLAUDE.md as existing precisely because Firestore rules can't prove the equivalent list-query policy — has zero test coverage of its own logic. `rules-tests/visibility.rules.test.ts` only proves that firestore.rules' list queries are unprovable/rejected (i.e. justifies why the routes exist), not that the routes' own TypeScript policy (owner-or-toss-passed-or-not-hidden-today) is correct. `src/services/dataService.test.ts` only has describe blocks for `getMatches` and `getEarliestMatchDate`; `getSquadsForMatch`/`getSquadsInDateRange`/`getVisibilitySettings` are never referenced. No `route.test.ts` exists anywhere under `src/app/api/`.
findings.notes: Verified via grep: `find src/app/api -name '*.test.ts'` returns nothing, and `grep -n 'getSquadsForMatch|getSquadsInDateRange' src/services/dataService.test.ts` returns nothing. Concrete fix: add a unit test that imports and calls the GET handlers in `src/app/api/leaderboard/route.ts` and `src/app/api/matches/[matchId]/squads/route.ts` directly (mocking `getAdminDb()`/`requireAuth()`), covering: (a) owner always sees their own squad even pre-toss on a hidden day, (b) a non-owner is denied a pre-toss squad on a hidden day, (c) a non-owner sees a post-toss squad regardless of the toggle, (d) a non-owner sees a squad on a non-hidden day pre-toss. This is exactly the matrix `rules-tests/squadWrite.rules.test.ts` uses for the write side — the read side's *application-code* reimplementation deserves the same rigor, especially since a regression here would silently leak or silently over-hide picks with no rules-engine safety net to catch it.

findings.finding: No CI configuration exists in the repository (no `.github/workflows/`, no other CI config found). `npm run test`, `npm run test:rules`, `npm run test:e2e`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` are all documented in CLAUDE.md/RUNBOOK.md as commands to run, but nothing runs them automatically on push or PR — they are purely manual, dependent on the maintainer (or an AI assistant) remembering to run RUNBOOK.md's 'Regular Health Check' before pushing.
findings.notes: Confirmed via `find . -iname '*.yml' -o -iname '*.yaml'` (excluding node_modules) turning up nothing and `.github` not existing. PROGRESS.md's own history includes an incident where a fix 'sat committed-but-unpushed... meaning main/Vercel production was still running the old code' for a day — a CI check that at least runs `npm run test && npm run lint && npm run build` on every push to main (or PR) would have made that class of drift visible immediately, and would catch a broken build/test/lint before it reaches Vercel's auto-deploy. Fix: add a minimal `.github/workflows/ci.yml` running `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, and `npm run test` on push/PR (the two emulator-dependent suites, `test:rules` and `test:e2e`, would need a JDK 21 setup step — see phase07-007 — so could be added as a second, allowed-to-be-slower job once that's sorted, or left manual if CI minutes are a concern for a hobby project).

findings.finding: `src/lib/scoring.test.ts`'s `validateScorecardResponse` describe block thoroughly unit-tests the Zod schema itself (accepts well-formed input, accepts passthrough of unknown fields, throws a named-field error on a retyped field, throws on a totally different shape) — but nothing tests that `POST /api/finalize-match` (src/app/api/finalize-match/route.ts) actually catches that thrown error and returns HTTP 502 with the field-naming message, since it's the route's own try/catch (lines ~44-48) doing that translation and no test imports/exercises the route handler directly.
findings.notes: This is a narrower, already partially self-disclosed gap: README.md's own 'Known Limitations' section says 'finalize-match isn't covered by an E2E test... the route handler itself is only manually verified,' so the project is aware finalize-match's route layer overall is untested — this finding just makes explicit that the specific fail-loud/502 contract CLAUDE.md highlights as a deliberate design choice ('deliberately refusing to compute scores rather than risk silently producing wrong points') is one of the untested parts of that route. Fix: a focused test that imports the route's POST handler with a mocked RapidAPI fetch returning a malformed scorecard (reusing the same malformed fixture from scoring.test.ts) and asserts the response status is 502 and the body's error message contains the expected field path — doesn't require hitting real RapidAPI or Firestore if `getAdminDb`/the RapidAPI client are mocked.

findings.finding: `npm run test:rules` fails to run in a real, currently-configured development environment: this machine has OpenJDK 17.0.19 installed, but running `npm run test:rules` fails with 'Error: firebase-tools no longer supports Java version before 21. Please install a JDK at version 21 or above.' `npm run test:e2e` would hit the identical blocker transitively since it also needs `npm run emulators` (same firebase-tools/JDK dependency).
findings.notes: The documentation is not wrong here — CLAUDE.md, RUNBOOK.md, and package.json's `emulators` script comment all already say 'needs Java 21+' — so this isn't a doc-accuracy bug. It's a DevEx/reliability gap: nothing in the repo verifies the Java version before attempting to run these suites, so the failure surfaces as an opaque firebase-tools crash rather than an early, friendly check, and — combined with phase07-005 (no CI) — means these two suites (29 rules tests + 8 E2E specs, per PROGRESS.md's most recent counts) can silently go unexercised for long stretches if whoever picks the project back up doesn't happen to have JDK 21+ already installed, exactly the 'comes back after a long break' scenario RUNBOOK.md is written for. Fix: add a short preflight check (e.g. a `predocker`/`pretest:rules` npm script running `java -version` and printing a clear 'install JDK 21+, see RUNBOOK.md' message before firebase-tools' own less-clear error fires), or note in RUNBOOK.md's health-check section that `java -version` should be checked first if `test:rules`/`test:e2e`/`emulators` fail with an unrelated-looking crash.

findings.finding: README.md's 'Project Structure' file tree (lines 47-154) lists CLAUDE.md, PROGRESS.md, RUNBOOK.md, and README.md itself as the project's top-level documentation files, but omits AGENTS.md entirely even though it exists at the repo root as a parallel AI-orientation doc for Codex.
findings.notes: Minor completeness gap in the file-structure listing, but worth fixing alongside phase07-001/003 since it means someone reading only README.md wouldn't know AGENTS.md exists or needs to be kept in sync with CLAUDE.md. Fix: add a line for AGENTS.md next to CLAUDE.md's entry, e.g. 'AGENTS.md — same content as CLAUDE.md, oriented for Codex.'

findings.finding: `npm run lint` (which CLAUDE.md, README.md, and RUNBOOK.md's Regular Health Check all document as the canonical lint command) invokes `next lint`, which now prints 'next lint is deprecated and will be removed in Next.js 16. ... migrate to the ESLint CLI.' Separately, `package.json` pins `eslint-config-next` to an exact version (`15.0.3`) while `next` itself floats on a caret range (`^15.5.20`) — every other dependency in the file uses a caret range, making this one exact pin (four minor versions behind the Next.js version actually in use) stand out as likely accidental rather than deliberate.
findings.notes: Both are currently harmless (lint passes clean: '✔ No ESLint warnings or errors') but are forward-looking DevEx risk: RUNBOOK.md tells a non-technical returning owner that 'What good looks like: ✔ No ESLint warnings or errors' for `npm run lint` — once Next.js 16 removes `next lint`, that exact command will stop working and the runbook step will need updating anyway. Fix: proactively migrate via `npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli .` (the exact command the deprecation warning itself suggests) before the Next.js 16 upgrade forces it, and change `eslint-config-next` to a caret range (`^15.5.20` or latest) to match the rest of the dependency list unless the exact pin was a deliberate workaround for a specific lint regression (undocumented if so).
